subject: website
name: Super Productivity
summary: A to-do list and time tracker, built from upstream's open source (MIT) at a pinned commit. Every script, bundled plugins included, ships in its own files, with no analytics: Level 3. Not Level 4: by default it asks api.github.com for the newest release when it opens and daily, an unverified connection the user did not start. Tasks stay on this computer; sync, trackers and calendars connect only once configured. Not private: GitHub sees your IP address on each check.

operations.name: Plan tasks and track time
operations.note: Kept in this site's browser storage on this computer, with no account.

operations.name: Sync between devices (WebDAV, SuperSync, Dropbox)
operations.note: Optional and off until configured. The code does what it promises, but the sync server holds the copy and sees your IP address and when you work.

operations.name: Import issues from a tracker or a calendar
operations.note: Optional and off until configured. The tracker or calendar server decides what is shown and sees your IP address.

connections.name: Update check (api.github.com)
connections.note: Made by default, after 30 seconds and then daily, unless turned off in Settings. It only decides whether a banner appears; the answer is not verified.

connections.name: Sync servers (WebDAV, SuperSync, Dropbox)
connections.note: Only the one the user configures. Answers are trusted as given.

connections.name: Issue trackers and calendars
connections.note: GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Redmine, Trello, ClickUp, Linear, OpenProject, Nextcloud Deck, CalDAV, Azure DevOps and iCal or Google calendars, each only when the user adds it.
